blocks.name: Different Types of Costs
blocks.definition: Total cost (TC), average total cost (ATC), fixed cost (FC), variable cost (VC), average fixed cost (AFC), average variable cost (AVC). Note: marginal cost is not required. Definition, drawing and interpretation of diagrams that show how changes in output affect costs of production.

blocks.md: - In preparing goods/services for sale, **firms incur a range of costs**. These costs can be be broken into different categories

1. **Fixed costs (FC) **are costs that do not change as the level of output changes

  - These have to be paid whether output is zero or 5000
  
    - E.g. Building rent, management salaries, insurance, bank loan repayments etc.
2. **Variable costs (VC) **are costs that vary directly with output

  - These increase as output increases and vice versa
  
    - E.g. raw material costs, wages of workers directly involved in production
3. **Total costs (TC) **are the sum of the fixed + total variable costs

blocks.name: Cost Calculations
blocks.definition: Calculation of TC, ATC, FC, VC, AFC and AVC.

blocks.md: - Based on the above definitions, we can calculate several different types of costs

1. $\mathrm{Total} \mathrm{costs}(\mathrm{TC})=\mathrm{total} \mathrm{fixed} \mathrm{costs}(\mathrm{TFC})+\mathrm{total} \mathrm{variable} \mathrm{costs}(\mathrm{TVC})$
2. $\mathrm{Total} \mathrm{variable} \mathrm{cost}(\mathrm{TVC})=\mathrm{variable} \mathrm{cost}(\mathrm{VC})\times\mathrm{quantity}(Q)$
3. $\mathrm{Average} \mathrm{total} \mathrm{cost}(\mathrm{AC})=\frac{\mathrm{total} \mathrm{cost}(\mathrm{TC})}{\mathrm{quantity}(Q)}$
4. $\mathrm{Average} \mathrm{fixed} \mathrm{cost}(\mathrm{AFC})=\frac{\mathrm{Total} \mathrm{fixed} \mathrm{costs}(\mathrm{TFC})}{\mathrm{quantity}(Q)}$
5. $\mathrm{Average} \mathrm{variable} \mathrm{cost}(\mathrm{AVC})=\frac{\mathrm{Total} \mathrm{variable} \mathrm{costs}(\mathrm{TVC})}{\mathrm{quantity}(Q)}$ ** **
**Cost Calculations Using the Above Formulas Where VC Is \$60**
**Sketches Which Represent the Different Costs of a Firm**

| **Type of Cost** | **Diagram** | **Explanation** | |---|---|---| | **Fixed Cost (FC)** | ![Graph showing fixed costs as a horizontal line at $4000 with cost on the vertical axis and output level on the horizontal axis.](assets/b8f2914ee51a-64978-httpscdn-savemyexams-comuploads2022113-7-1.png) | - The firm has to pay its ***fixed costs*** which do not change, irrespective if the output is 0 or 100,000 units
- The fixed costs for this firm are \$4,000 | | **Variable Cost (VC)** | ![Graph showing the relationship between total variable costs and output level with a red upward-sloping line, labelled axes in dollars and output.](assets/c7c23dc6ade0-3656-httpscdn-savemyexams-comuploads2022113-7-2-.png) | - The variable costs initially **rise proportionally with output**, as shown in the diagram
- At some point the firm will benefit from a ***purchasing economy of scale*** and the rise will no longer be proportional | | **Total Cost (TC)** | ![Graph showing costs versus output level with three lines: fixed cost (horizontal), variable cost (diagonal), and total cost (steeper diagonal).](assets/28cde0f41089-26892-httpscdn-savemyexams-comuploads202211-zxig.png) | - The **total cost** is the sum of the variable and fixed costs
- The total costs **cannot be 0** as all firms have some level of fixed costs | | **Average Fixed Cost (AFC)** | ![Graph showing average fixed cost curve, downward sloping from left to right. Y-axis is labelled "Costs ($)" and X-axis "Output Level".](assets/16c43d3c4854-44524-httpscdn-savemyexams-comuploads2022113-7-2.png) | - If the **fixed costs** of a firm are \$1,000 and it produces 1 unit of output, then its **AFC is \$1,000** (\$1,000/1)
- If the firm increases its output to 1000 units, then the **AFC is \$1 per unit **(\$1000/1,000)
- The **more units** a firm produces, the **lower its AFC** will be
- This is one reasons why large levels of output help to increase the **profit per unit** | | **Average Total Cost (AC)** | ![Graph showing average total cost curve, costs on vertical axis, output level on horizontal axis. Curve dips from point a and rises after point b.](assets/0413fc85b8ad-8692-httpscdn-savemyexams-comuploads2022113-7-2-.png) | - As a firm grows, it is able to increases its **scale of output **generating efficiencies that lower its **average total costs (AC)** of production
- These efficiencies are called ***economies of scale***
- As a firm continues increasing its **scale of output**, it will reach a point where its **average total costs (AC)** will start to **increase**
- The reasons for the increase in the average costs are called ***diseconomies of scale*** |

blocks.md: MCQ frequently tests your knowledge of these curves by presenting you with 4 unlabelled diagrams and, for example, asking you to identify which sketch demonstrates the average fixed costs of the firm.

blocks.name: Different Types of Revenue
blocks.definition: Total revenue (TR) and average revenue (AR). Note: marginal revenue is not required. Calculation of TR and AR. The influence of sales on revenue.

blocks.md: - **Total revenue** is the total value of all sales a firm incurs
- **Average revenue** is the overall revenue per unit

- **Average revenue** information is especially useful to a firm **selling multiple products** (e.g. supermarkets) or a firm that sells the **same item at different prices** (e.g. rail tickets are usually priced differently for different types of commuters e.g. pensioners)
